title: Computation Note on the Payoff Amount of a Past-Due Fee Invoice — Contingency Placement Agreements
content:
**Payoff.** Under the Contingency Placement Agreements, the payoff of a past-due fee invoice is the invoice's unpaid amount plus every late charge booked on that invoice, rounded to the cent.

**Unpaid amount.** The invoice's unpaid amount for the payoff is the invoice amount less the fee payments and fee credits applied to that invoice, and never less than zero.

## Where each figure comes from

All figures are read from the agreement's client money history, by the number of the invoice being paid off:

| Figure | Entries |
|---|---|
| Invoice amount | the fee invoice entry |
| Fee payments applied | fee payment entries carrying the invoice number |
| Fee credits applied | fee credit entries carrying the invoice number |
| Late charges on the invoice | late-charge entries carrying the invoice number |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

Invoice amount 2400.00 USD; fee payments applied 600.00 USD; fee credits applied 150.00 USD; late charges on the invoice of 24.75 USD, 26.10 USD and 27.00 USD.

- Unpaid amount: 2400.00 USD less 600.00 USD less 150.00 USD, which is 1650.00 USD.
- Late charges on the invoice: 24.75 USD plus 26.10 USD plus 27.00 USD, which is 77.85 USD.
- Payoff: 1650.00 USD plus 77.85 USD, which is 1727.85 USD.

An invoice of 500.00 USD with payments of 300.00 USD and a credit of 250.00 USD has an unpaid amount of zero, not a negative figure; with one late charge of 5.00 USD on it, its payoff is 5.00 USD.
